title: Verifier‑Grounded Evaluation of LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: A Preregistered Paired Test of paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (shared_initial_candidate)
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, artifact‑anchored paired experiment (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37) that compares a deterministic template baseline to a single‑pass LLM generator (declared_model_version = gpt‑5‑mini) on N = 120 synthetic intent→configuration tasks evaluated by a deterministic validator. The preregistered estimand was paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline under generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (a single canonical LLM candidate per pair reused for both scoring conditions). Under these frozen confirmatory semantics all episodes completed and passed the verifier: baseline = 120/120; guarded (gpt‑5‑mini, canonical seed_0) = 120/120; paired difference = 0.00; 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729); McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. We publish the complete execution and analysis artifacts (execution/execution_manifest.json and per‑file SHA‑256 fingerprints) and use them to (i) diagnose—artifact‑grounded—why the preregistered design produced a degenerate but correct paired outcome (identical inputs + deterministic validator), and (ii) provide runnable, artifact‑grounded protocol modifications (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed confirmatory design, validator diversity) that yield informative operational comparisons while preserving byte‑for‑byte reproducibility. The immutable initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba).

sections.introduction: Automating intent→configuration translation is central to NetOps; safety depends on semantic correctness (reachability, ACL/routing policy preservation, and safe transient workflows). Deterministic validators (Batfish class) provide auditable pre‑deployment checks and have become operational oracles for proposed configuration artifacts [https://doi.org/10.1145/3603269.3604866]. Large language models (LLMs) promise faster intent→config synthesis, but their stochastic outputs raise operational questions: what is the independent probability that an LLM candidate satisfies deterministic verifier constraints? To answer a narrowly specified estimand and to practice transparent reproducibility, we preregistered CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1. The preregistered primary hypothesis (H1) tested whether a single‑pass LLM pipeline (gpt‑5‑mini) has a lower paired verifier pass rate than a deterministic template baseline, using a paired design with generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (one canonical candidate generated and reused for both scoring conditions). Here we summarize the preregistered design, execution artifacts, confirmatory results, and an artifact‑grounded diagnosis of why the confirmatory contingency collapsed to a degenerate but correct outcome. We then present immediate runnable, artifact‑anchored modifications to measure the operational quantity operators usually want (independent generative reliability).
sections.related_work: Verifier‑grounded NetOps evaluation. Offline semantic validators and configuration analyzers (Batfish and related formal approaches) are established tools for pre‑deployment verification; they compute forwarding/reachability and detect policy violations from static configurations and scale to realistic networks [Brown et al., 2023; DOI:10.1145/3603269.3604866]. Recent LLM→NetOps work follows the generate–validate–repair pattern: a generator proposes candidates, a verifier checks deterministic semantic properties, and an iterative repair loop attempts fixes. Empirical studies of repair loops report diminishing returns after a few iterations and highlight orchestration/feedback design as a dominant factor in repair effectiveness (see the iterative repair literature in our evidence bundle). Methodological axes that materially affect measured reliability include sampling semantics (single canonical candidate vs. independent per‑condition sampling), repair budget, and validator scope. The present work contributes by preregistering the estimand explicitly (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline under shared_initial_candidate) and publishing exhaustive artifacts (provider calls, responses, validator traces, and SHA‑256 fingerprints) to enable deterministic reruns and auditable diagnosis.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen plan. The study was preregistered as CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1 (SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37) before observing model outputs. Key confirmatory choices: paired design, N = 120 tasks (40 per topology class: edge, datacenter, multi‑AS), primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (one canonical LLM candidate per task reused for both scoring conditions), initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1, maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1, deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version 5.0), and analysis via paired_binary_analysis_v1 (10,000 bootstrap resamples, seed = 1729). The full preregistration is archived in the artifact bundle and referenced above. Task synthesis. Tasks were programmatically synthesized from deterministic templates (generator_id deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5, version 5.0). Each task manifest entry encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, an explicit required_sequence, per‑task workflow_policies (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields, minimum_active_in_groups), allowed_touched_fields, and difficulty annotations. Representative task manifests and canonical candidates are archived under execution/task_manifest.jsonl and execution/responses/* (examples: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 8f38c8becd7e1e36..., task-000002-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 ae967f70dfb6ccb8..., task-000003-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 f7f4db249ecbbce...). Model and orchestration. The declared LLM in the preregistration and execution was gpt‑5‑mini accessed via adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1 (see execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Because generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate", model_calls_used = 120 (one canonical generation per task) although planned_episode_count = 240 (each canonical candidate was scored twice—baseline and guarded). All provider call traces are archived under execution/provider_calls/*.json and execution/call_cache/* to permit exact replay. Deterministic validator and scoring. Each candidate was evaluated by deterministic_netops_validator_v5 operating in full_intent_constraint_validation mode (binary pass requires all required commands and transient constraints to be satisfied). The validator emits a JSON trace per episode (execution/scoring/*.json). Representative validator trace: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256 0d56c1add7c5a57f...). Execution accounting and retries. Planned_episode_count = 240; completed_episode_count = 240; failed_episode_count = 0; model_calls_used = 120; maximum_model_calls = 240. A preregistered retry policy allowed up to two automated retries for infrastructure failures; none were required. Contamination heuristics (exact‑match and normalized n‑gram overlap) were run and recorded (analysis/contamination_summary.csv), but string overlap is only a heuristic for pretraining exposure. Reproducibility artifacts. The complete execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json) lists every produced file and its SHA‑256 fingerprint; researchers may reproduce byte‑for‑byte runs using those paths and hashes. The immutable initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba).
sections.results: Confirmatory counts and exactly archived statistics. All preregistered confirmatory episodes completed and are archived. Observed counts: baseline_success_count = 120/120; guarded_success_count (gpt‑5‑mini, canonical seed_0) = 120/120; complete_pair_count = 120. The paired contingency table is therefore n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 9f25790c7eeaafb3562e0710e0cf10b7a47a55ea00fcbcf02eee324f79afafe7). Primary estimand and inference (preregistered). The paired estimator (mean over pairs of guarded_i − baseline_i) = 0.00. The preregistered percentile bootstrap (10,000 replicates, seed = 1729) yields a 95% CI [0.00, 0.00]; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. All analysis artifacts and figures are archived (analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg SHA‑256 ae5b8e0c644f8cf7...). Representative validator traces. Each scoring JSON includes parsed_command_count, required_command_count, normalized_configuration, transient checks and final_state. Example: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256 0d56c1add7c5a57f...) records parsed_command_count = 4, required_command_count = 4 and validation_after.valid = true; the canonical candidate used is execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 8f38c8becd7e1e36...). Root‑cause diagnosis (artifact grounded). The confirmatory contingency collapsed because two preregistered, archived choices combined deterministically: (1) generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" produced a single canonical candidate per task and that canonical candidate was reused verbatim for both baseline and guarded scoring episodes (see execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt files, SHA‑256s above), and (2) the deterministic validator enforces the task templates' explicit required_sequences and workflow_policies; identical inputs must yield identical validator outputs. Thus the observed 120/120, 120/120 outcome is a correct measurement of the preregistered estimand (validator consistency under identical inputs), not of independent per‑condition generative reliability.
sections.discussion: What was measured and what remains unanswered. The preregistered confirmatory test correctly answered its estimand—whether a deterministic validator treats identical canonical candidates differently across scoring conditions; the answer is no. It does not, however, estimate the operational quantity most practitioners require: the independent probability that an LLM, sampled independently, produces a verifier‑passing configuration. That operational quantity requires independent per‑condition sampling (different seeds per condition) or multi‑seed sampling per condition; the published artifacts permit deterministically reproducible reruns that implement those semantics without altering the original task definitions. Runnable, artifact‑grounded next experiments. Because every relevant artifact is archived (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 a40e96e2..., execution/task_manifest.jsonl, execution/provider_calls/*, execution/responses/*, execution/scoring/*), the following deterministic reruns are immediately executable: (A) independent_per_condition rerun: generate a distinct seed per condition per task (baseline seed_0, guarded seed_1), rescore with deterministic_netops_validator_v5, and recompute paired contrasts; (B) multi‑seed confirmatory design: draw K ≥ 3 independent seeds per condition and estimate per‑condition pass probability with bootstrap CIs; (C) validator diversification: run a second verifier and report intersection/union pass rates to reduce validator–task coupling. Because the call cache and provider traces are archived, these reruns yield auditable outputs. Threats to validity (artifact‑visible). Internal validity: the shared_initial design intentionally removed generation variance and therefore precluded testing independent generative reliability. Construct validity: template‑aligned tasks and single deterministic validator increase the chance that canonical candidates satisfy required_sequences, possibly overstating success relative to open natural language intents. External validity: a single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) and synthetic templates limit generalization. Conclusion validity: a degenerate contingency produces trivial but correct inferential outputs; interpreting them beyond their precise estimand is incorrect. Operational implications. Two practical lessons emerge: (1) pair the experimental generation semantics to the operational question before executing a run (shared canonical candidates test validator determinism; independent sampling tests generative reliability); (2) publish exhaustive artifacts (provider calls, canonical candidates, validator traces, SHA‑256 manifest) to permit deterministic reruns and unambiguous post‑hoc diagnosis. Our bundle exemplifies both points and supplies the artifacts necessary for follow‑up confirmatory runs.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, verifier‑grounded paired experiment and released a complete, byte‑for‑byte reproducible artifact bundle (execution/execution_manifest.json and per‑file SHA‑256s). Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics both the deterministic template baseline and the gpt‑5‑mini guarded condition validated on all N = 120 tasks (120/120 each). Archived evidence shows that identical canonical candidates per pair and template‑tight task constraints caused the degenerate contingency; thus the confirmatory paired result does not provide evidence about independent LLM generative reliability. We publish runnable, artifact‑grounded protocols (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed replication, validator diversification) that answer the operational question without sacrificing reproducibility. The immutable initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba).

limitations: Controlled synthetic tasks: programmatic templates produced narrow required_sequences and workflow_policies that favour canonical solutions and limit external generalizability to heterogeneous operational intents.

Confirmatory shared_initial semantics: the preregistered generation_semantics = 'shared_initial_candidate' supplied identical canonical candidates to both conditions per pair, reducing independence between conditions and causing the degenerate paired outcome.

Single canonical seed for confirmatory test: the primary analysis used one canonical seed per task; preregistered exploratory multi‑seed analyses (seeds_1..4) were not included in the confirmatory inference reported here.

Validator–task coupling: the deterministic validator enforces constraints encoded in the task templates, which can increase pass rates for template‑aligned candidates and reduce construct validity for open distributions.

Possible training‑data exposure: preregistered contamination heuristics found no flags under chosen thresholds, but absence of a flag is not proof of zero exposure to related artifacts in model pretraining.

Single‑model, single‑validator run: results apply only to gpt‑5‑mini under the recorded configuration and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; they do not generalize across model families, agentic pipelines, or other validators.
